walkthroughs.body_html:
The KS3 reactivity series from most to least reactive:

K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, C, Zn, Fe, H, Cu, Ag, Au

Carbon and hydrogen are non-metals included for comparison.

The top metals (K, Na, Ca) react vigorously with water. Magnesium reacts with steam. Iron reacts slowly. Gold barely reacts at all.

Higher up = more reactive.

Try: Please Stop Calling My Aunt Charlie's Zebra In Her Caravan, Sell-out Aunt.

Or make your own! Anything that helps you remember K Na Ca Mg Al C Zn Fe H Cu Ag Au.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.

mcqs.q: How does the rate of an SN2 reaction depend on concentrations?
options: Rate is first order in both substrate AND nucleophile (overall second order) because both are involved in the rate-determining step.
SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
SN2 reactions are first order overall because only the substrate matters.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
SN2 reactions are zero order because they happen in one step.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
